findings.reason: a node told to put the census check in `supervise` puts it in a function holding no per-child state and no exit status, and the gate it writes there cannot observe a restart.
findings.text: §5 says "`supervise` (`reckon/crew/session_host.py` near line 625) restarts a child that exits other than settled", but `supervise` is at line 648 and is only the select/read loop; every restart is decided in `tick()` (`reckon/crew/session_host.py:512`–566), where the exit is collected (`_poll_exit`, 568) and the new pid spawned (558)

findings.reason: the node would land a second guard beside one that already covers the restart and defeat neither, so §5's 0.75 h produces no change in the behaviour its evidence describes unless the section says which residual state (census child present but registration not live) it is for.
findings.text: §5's mechanism cannot produce the outcome §1 records, and the guard it adds partly exists: §1's evidence is that nova-8a's own host "still listed no child", so "settle the child when another live host's census already serves the pair" would not have stopped the replacement pid 1076196; and `tick()` already refuses to spawn that replacement when a live follower this host did not start holds the pair (`_foreign_live_follower`, reckon/crew/session_host.py:460, consulted at 553), deferring rather than restarting

response_events.note: §5 is removed. tick() (session_host.py near line 512) already defers rather than restarts when a foreign live follower holds the pair (_foreign_live_follower, near line 460); the replacement in §1 came from a host holding a pair it should never have been asked for, which §3 prevents; and a host cannot tell which sessions its owner holds, since one host serves both a Claude session id and a crew session name. §1 now says so.
